name: Sable Charge
description: Sable Charge is a world of black rock and red fire, its surface an endless mosaic of cooled lava fields split by glowing fissures that reveal molten rivers beneath. Four supervolcanoes dominate the northern hemisphere, their eruption columns rising through the toxic atmosphere like pillars holding up a ceiling of perpetual ash cloud. Where the crust has fractured most severely, the planet's iron-nickel core is partially exposed, a blinding white-orange glow visible from orbit.

The toxic atmosphere reeks of sulfur dioxide and hydrogen chloride, a cocktail that corrodes unprotected metal within hours and dissolves organic material in minutes. Acid rain falls in sheets across the equatorial zones, carving intricate dissolution patterns into the basalt that almost resemble script. The ground trembles constantly with seismic activity, a vibration so pervasive that returning miners report feeling phantom tremors for weeks after departure.

A mining corporation established an extraction complex here decades ago, drawn by the extraordinary concentration of heavy metals near the exposed core. The complex was abandoned after a series of eruptions destroyed the primary processing facility and irradiated the surrounding area with material dredged from deep within the mantle. Extremophilic microbes thrive in the acid pools and thermal vents, their biochemistry so alien that they have been classified as a parallel genesis event.

Sable Charge's mineral wealth remains tantalizing, with automated surveys confirming titanium and uranium deposits that dwarf most known reserves. The abandoned mining complex still contains salvageable equipment, but the radiation hotspots surrounding it require specialized shielding. The microbial life forms have begun appearing in unexpected locations, spreading along the cooling edges of new lava flows with a rapidity that suggests either remarkable adaptation or directed migration.
